name: TEAC
usb_vendor_ids_source: Linux kernel USB audio quirk tables, sound/usb/quirks.c (d2636407bf8c, 2026-11-12) and sound/usb/quirks-table.h (e7c66b3e249e, 2026-11-04)
_refused: Read 2026-11-25 at https://teac.jp/int/terms, the terms page linked from the footer of TEAC Corporation's own site - the host that serves the UD, NT and Reference product pages at teac.jp/int/product/<model>/spec. The prohibiting clause, under « Copyrights, Trademarks, etc. »: « Other than for personal use or other fair use explicitly allowed by law, you are prohibited to use the Content (including downloading, reproduction, change, uploading, posting, transmission, distribution, licensing, sale, and publication) without obtaining the Company's prior written permission. » It defines what it covers: « Copyrights to the texts, images, sounds, programs, and other works contained in this website (hereinafter collectively referred to as "Content") are owned by the Company, the respective original authors, or other right holders thereof. » And it grants nothing by default: « The Company and its affiliates do not grant any license to use or exercise any copyrights, patents, trademarks, and any other intellectual property rights, unless individually and expressly specified otherwise. » A third clause, under « Prohibited Conduct », lists among the forbidden acts: « Acts aimed for business activities, profits, or preparations for such business activities; » Footer: « Copyright 2026 TEAC Corporation All Rights Reserved. » robots.txt carries no Content-Signal and names no Claude agent - a single « User-Agent:* » group ending « Allow:/ » - so the product pages are not blocked technically; the prohibition is entirely in the terms. No product page was opened beyond its footer, and no record will exist under this brand.
_the_Esoteric_precedent_held: This harvest was sent out expecting a refusal, because Esoteric - TEAC's own high-end brand - has been in this catalogue's register since the first week, with terms that forbid reusing site content. The prediction was that a shared parent carries shared terms, and it was right. Worth recording as a prediction that paid off, because the register's two predictors - a maker who treats its documentation as a product, and a maker selling through a platform whose default terms forbid reuse - now have a third beside them: A SIBLING BRAND ALREADY IN THE REGISTER. It is the cheapest of the three to check and it costs one lookup.
_what_is_lost: Everything, and this is one of the costliest refusals in the register. Left unread on teac.jp: UD-507 and UD-701N (USB DACs), NT-507T (network player), VRDS-701, VRDS-701T, PD-507T, PD-301-X, AI-303, AX-505, AP-505, AP-507, AP-701, HA-507, PE-505, CD-P750DAB and a discontinued-products section. TEAC publishes named digital filters AND a user-selectable upsampling with an OFF position, which almost no other maker does and which is precisely what `correctable` and `device_settings` exist for. It also states native DSD and DoP separately. A written permission here would be worth more to this catalogue than any other single grant.
_the_distributor_host_is_a_different_mat: eu.teac-audio.com is NOT TEAC: its imprint names « ATS trade&service GmbH, Moslbichl 78, A-6250 Kundl, Austria » and « Responsible for Content Due to § 6 MDStV: ATS trade&service GmbH », with a footer « (c) 2026 ATS trade&service GmbH ». Its terms page carries no site terms of use at all - its whole body is a link to a sales-terms PDF - whose § 11.3 reads « The customer agrees to neither duplicate nor pass on to third parties texts, sketches, drawings, pictures, photographs and other ATS content unless explicitly marked for general distribution by ATS (e.g. catalogue). » Not harvested, and NOT ONLY because of that clause: § 2.4 says « The dimensions, weights, illustrations, descriptions and other information stated in catalogues, brochures and other documents or on the website are only approximate and subject to change, unless the nature of such information is stated as absolute explicitly and in writing. » A source that declares its own figures approximate by default disqualifies itself as a specification source regardless of permission. That is a NEW reason to reject a source in this catalogue - not « may we » but « is this a fact at all » - and it argues for always preferring the maker's own host over a distributor's, even where the distributor permits and the maker forbids.
_the_other_hosts_measured: teac.com is not an audio site: it 301-redirects to datarecorder.teac.com, TEAC America's data-recorder division, which carries no converters and whose index.php returned 404; its robots.txt is 404, so no Content-Signal could be checked there. The US audio site is dead - teac.jp/us/terms 302s to audio.teac.com, which does not resolve - so no US terms page exists to read. teac-audio.eu refuses connections on both 443 and 80. And teacaudio.com is a third-party lookalike: it returns 200 with Italian marketing prose, no imprint, no legal pages and no TEAC Corporation footer, so it is not a maker source and was not harvested.
_it_can_be_lifted: Conditioned on « the Company's prior written permission ». On the letter list, and near the top of it: see _what_is_lost. Two practical notes for whoever harvests after a grant - on teac.jp/int/product/ud-507/feature the SPECIFICATIONS, DOWNLOADS and FAQ tabs are javascript:void(0) placeholders that a plain fetcher cannot open, and the specifications have their own /spec URL that must be fetched directly.
